_comment: Causes confirmed by reading the installed source of each flagged indicator. Paths are relative to site-packages. An entry applies only to the listed version; a flagged indicator without a matching entry is reported as unconfirmed.

ta/trend.KSTIndicator.cause: Each rate of change is computed against close.shift(r, fill_value=close.mean()), so the first r rows are compared with the mean of the whole series, future included. With the default windows the contaminated values are KST rows 14-43 and signal rows 14-51 (the first 14 rows are missing); later rows are clean.
ta/trend.KSTIndicator.documentation: Not mentioned in the class docstring (ta/trend.py:440-462). The same fill was reported for the daily-return indicator (bukosabino/ta issue 323) and removed there (pull request 324, merged 2023-10-29); the KST lines are unchanged on the master branch as of 2026-11-15.

finta/ICHIMOKU.cause: The Chikou span is ohlc['close'].shift(-chikou_period): the value at row t is the close 26 rows later. This is the standard definition of the span, which is drawn 26 bars behind price on a chart.
finta/ICHIMOKU.documentation: The docstring (finta/finta.py:1857-1862) does not say that the column holds future closes.

finta/QSTICK.classification: output depends on input length, no future values read
finta/QSTICK.cause: The function takes ohlc['close'].tail(period) and ohlc['open'].tail(period) and returns (close - open) / period for those rows only. It is not a rolling average: the output exists for the last 14 rows of whatever frame is passed, so the value at row t depends on how many rows follow it. The values themselves use only the row's own open and close.
finta/QSTICK.documentation: The docstring (finta/finta.py:1771-1773) describes an average over the past N days.

finta/SAR.cause: The recursion is seeded with low[0] - (high - low).std(), the standard deviation of the bar range over the whole series. The seed enters each later value through the recursion. The dependence ends once the path has reversed and resynchronised: a reversal sets the value to the running extreme, which does not involve the seed. Only observable on an integer index: on a date index the function raises KeyError under pandas 3.1 because of high[0].

finta/STOCHRSI.cause: RSI is scaled as (rsi - rsi.min()) / (rsi.max() - rsi.min()) with the minimum and maximum of the whole series, not of the trailing stoch_period window, and then smoothed. Every value changes whenever a later RSI sets a new extreme.
finta/STOCHRSI.documentation: The docstring (finta/finta.py:1231-1233) describes the range 'over a set time period'.

finta/WILLIAMS_FRACTAL.cause: Both outputs use rolling(window=2 * period + 1, center=True), so the flag at row t reads period = 2 rows after t. A fractal is defined by the bars on both sides of it.
finta/WILLIAMS_FRACTAL.documentation: finta/finta.py:2211: period is 'how many lower highs/higher lows the extremum value should be preceded and followed'.

pandas_ta_classic/overlap.ichimoku.cause: chikou_span = close.shift(-kijun); include_chikou defaults to True.
pandas_ta_classic/overlap.ichimoku.documentation: pandas_ta_classic/overlap/ichimoku.py:146-148 and 156-157: 'Not causal: the chikou span is close.shift(-kijun), a later bar's close'; lookahead=False drops the column.

pandas_ta_classic/statistics.tos_stdeval.cause: One regression line (np.polyfit) and one standard deviation are fitted over the whole series and returned for every row.
pandas_ta_classic/statistics.tos_stdeval.documentation: pandas_ta_classic/statistics/tos_stdevall.py:102-109: 'Not causal. A single linear regression is fitted over the whole window'; lookahead=False returns None with a warning.

pandas_ta_classic/trend.dpo.cause: With centered=True (the default) the result is (close.shift(t) - sma).shift(-t) with t = int(0.5 * length) + 1 = 11, so the value at row t uses the moving average ending 11 rows later.
pandas_ta_classic/trend.dpo.documentation: pandas_ta_classic/trend/dpo.py:76-78 and 82-84: 'Not causal: the value at a bar uses the SMA ending int(0.5 * length) + 1 bars later'; lookahead=False turns centring off.

btalib/ht_trendmode.cause: Index handling. The working series passed to _periodize have their first 6 rows removed, so on an integer index their labels start at 6. Scalar reads and writes such as price[i] and trendbuf[i] = trend are then label-based, while the trendline sum price0[i - (dcperiod - 1):i + 1] is a positional slice that ends 6 rows later. The trend flag written at label i therefore depends on prices up to row i + 6, and the last 6 rows are never written. Only observable on an integer index: on a date index the function raises KeyError under pandas 3.1.
btalib/ht_trendmode.documentation: Not documented; the code is written as if all access were positional.

ta[fillna=True]/momentum.KAMAIndicator.cause: The volatility and efficiency-ratio terms use np.roll, which wraps around: the first rows are differenced against the last rows of the series. With fillna=False the affected rows are masked (the rolling sum has min_periods=window and the first valid KAMA value is set to the close). With fillna=True min_periods is 0, the wrapped values enter the smoothing constant of rows 1-9, and the recursion carries the error forward with decaying size.
ta[fillna=True]/momentum.KAMAIndicator.documentation: Not documented. Reported upstream in 2020 (bukosabino/ta issue 181, still open).

ta[fillna=True]/trend.DPOIndicator.cause: close.shift(11, fill_value=close.mean()) puts the mean of the whole series in the first 11 rows. With fillna=False those rows are missing because the moving average has min_periods=window; with fillna=True min_periods is 0 and rows 0-10 are returned.

ta[fillna=True]/trend.KSTIndicator.cause: Same cause as with the default: close.shift(r, fill_value=close.mean()). With fillna=True the rolling means have min_periods=0, so the contaminated values start at row 0.

ta[fillna=True]/trend.TRIXIndicator.cause: ema3.shift(1, fill_value=ema3.mean()) puts the mean of the whole triple-smoothed series in row 0. With fillna=False row 0 is missing; with fillna=True the moving averages have min_periods=0 and row 0 is returned.

ta[fillna=True]/trend.VortexIndicator.cause: The true range of row 0 is computed against close.shift(1, fill_value=close.mean()). With fillna=False the first 14 rows are missing and row 0 never enters a returned value; with fillna=True the rolling sums have min_periods=0 and rows 0-13 include it.
